## Executive Summary

Mixin (buildVersion 0.8.7 at the pinned commit) is the bytecode-patching standard of the entire
modding ecosystem: both loader families ship it (Fabric bundles a pinned fork, FML integrates it
via an advice provider — see those dossiers), and tens of thousands of mods depend on its
semantics. It lets mods declare bytecode changes as annotated Java classes — @Mixin targets a
class; @Shadow/@Final/@Mutable mirror members; @Overwrite replaces; the injector family
(@Inject, @Redirect, @ModifyArg/@ModifyArgs, @ModifyVariable, @ModifyConstant) surgically
patches method bodies at declarative injection points (@At + @Slice selectors) — and merges
those changes into target classes at load time through a transformer pipeline.

Three architectural properties matter most for OmniLoader. First, the **service abstraction**
(IMixinService + a dozen sibling SPIs): Mixin does not know what loader hosts it — bytecode
access, class trees, transformer chaining, logging, and even an audit trail are all injected by
the host. This is precisely the seam OmniLoader implements to host Mixin natively. Second,
**reference maps** (refmaps): injector target strings are written against dev-time names and
remapped to runtime names via generated JSON — the mechanism that couples every Mixin-using mod
to its ecosystem's mapping universe, and thus a hard input to Omni's cross-ecosystem remapping
(Sinytra's pipeline exists partly to rewrite these). Third, **environment/compatibility
levels**: configs declare minimum Mixin versions and JVM compat levels, letting one runtime
serve a decade of mods — the versioning discipline Omni's own transformation SPI must match.

## Architecture Components

### Declaration model (annotations)

- **Location**: `src/main/java/org/spongepowered/asm/mixin/ + gen/`
- **Role**: Bytecode patches expressed as annotated Java classes
- **Sources**: `annotations`, `gen`

A mixin class @Mixin-targets one or more classes (including by string for non-public targets
and @Pseudo for possibly-absent ones). @Shadow mirrors existing members for compile-time-safe
references; @Overwrite documents whole-method replacement; @Unique namespaces added members;
@Accessor/@Invoker generate synthetic bridges to private members. Because patches are ordinary
Java, they get IDE/type safety — the property that made Mixin the ecosystem standard over raw
ASM, and the bar any Omni-native patching story must clear.

### Injector framework

- **Location**: `src/main/java/org/spongepowered/asm/mixin/injection/ + points/`
- **Role**: Surgical method-body patching at declarative injection points
- **Sources**: `injectors`, `injection-points`

Injectors bind handler methods into target method bodies: @Inject (callbacks with cancellation
support at HEAD/RETURN/INVOKE/FIELD/etc.), @Redirect (replace a call/field access), @ModifyArg,
@ModifyArgs, @ModifyVariable, @ModifyConstant. @At selectors with @Slice ranges and @Desc
descriptors locate targets; InjectionPoint is itself extensible for custom point types. The
injector semantics — especially multi-mod stacking on one target and priority ordering — are
the de-facto contract OmniLoader must preserve bit-for-bit for hosted mods.

### Transformer/application pipeline

- **Location**: `src/main/java/org/spongepowered/asm/mixin/transformer/`
- **Role**: Selects applicable mixins per class and merges them at load time
- **Sources**: `transformer`, `environment`

MixinConfig models each mixins.json (targets, priority, plugin, refmap, compat level);
ClassInfo maintains a metadata model of the class hierarchy without loading classes;
MixinApplicatorStandard merges members, applies injectors, and validates; coprocessors
(e.g. accessor support) run alongside. MixinEnvironment sequences phases (preinit/init/default)
and sides. Application is priority-ordered across all configs targeting a class — the
multi-mod-stacking behavior at the heart of ecosystem compatibility.

### Service abstraction (host SPI)

- **Location**: `src/main/java/org/spongepowered/asm/service/`
- **Role**: Everything loader-specific is injected: bytecode access, transformers, audit, logging
- **Sources**: `service-spi`

IMixinService + siblings (IClassBytecodeProvider, ITransformerProvider, IClassTracker,
IGlobalPropertyService, IMixinAuditTrail…) define what a host loader must provide. Fabric's
MixinServiceKnot and FML's advice-provider integration (see those dossiers) are both
implementations of this SPI. For OmniLoader the conclusion is direct: implement one
MixinServiceOmni over the native transformation pipeline and every hosted ecosystem's mixins
run through one audited path.

### Reference maps (refmaps)

- **Location**: `src/main/java/org/spongepowered/asm/mixin/refmap/`
- **Role**: Remap injector target strings from dev names to runtime names
- **Sources**: `refmap`

Injector targets are strings resolved against a generated refmap JSON per environment;
RemappingReferenceMapper applies the active mapping context at runtime. This is where mods
bind to their ecosystem's namespace (intermediary for Fabric, official for NeoForge) — and
therefore exactly what cross-ecosystem translation must rewrite (Sinytra's transformer does).
Omni's compat pipeline must translate refmaps per hosted ecosystem as a first-class step.

### Config plugins (extensibility)

- **Location**: `src/main/java/org/spongepowered/asm/mixin/extensibility/`
- **Role**: Programmatic per-config control at application time
- **Sources**: `extensibility`

IMixinConfigPlugin lets a mod filter/augment its own mixins at runtime (shouldApplyMixin,
target list manipulation, post-apply hooks) — widely used for conditional compat patches.
Any hosted-Mixin implementation must run these plugins faithfully; they execute arbitrary
mod code during transformation, which is also a sandboxing consideration for OmniLoader.

## Feature Inventory

### architecture

| Feature | Maturity | Future-proofing | Omni relevance | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Loader-agnostic service SPI | core | 5/5 | adopt | `service-spi` |

**Loader-agnostic service SPI** — All environment specifics (bytecode access, transformer chain, audit, logging) are injected via IMixinService implementations.

*Omni notes*: OmniLoader ships MixinServiceOmni over its native pipeline — one integration point, every ecosystem's mixins.

### bytecode

| Feature | Maturity | Future-proofing | Omni relevance | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Declarative injector model | core | 5/5 | adopt | `injectors`, `injection-points` |
| Hierarchy metadata without classloading (ClassInfo) | core | 4/5 | adapt | `transformer` |

**Declarative injector model** — Method-body patches as annotations with extensible injection points, priority stacking, and cancellation semantics.

*Omni notes*: The ecosystem contract. Omni preserves semantics exactly; native Omni mods get the same tool rather than a competing invention.

**Hierarchy metadata without classloading (ClassInfo)** — A parallel class-metadata model answers hierarchy/member queries without triggering class loads.

*Omni notes*: The load-order-safety trick every transformation pipeline eventually needs; Omni's pipeline should build this once, centrally.

### compat

| Feature | Maturity | Future-proofing | Omni relevance | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Refmap-based target remapping | core | 4/5 | adopt | `refmap` |
| Compatibility levels + phased environment | core | 4/5 | adopt | `environment`, `transformer` |

**Refmap-based target remapping** — Injector target strings resolve through generated per-environment reference maps at runtime.

*Omni notes*: Hard dependency for hosting: Omni's per-ecosystem translation must rewrite or re-resolve refmaps (Sinytra precedent).

**Compatibility levels + phased environment** — Configs pin minimum versions and JVM compat levels; application is phased (preinit/init/default) and side-aware.

*Omni notes*: How one runtime serves a decade of mods. Omni's transformation SPI adopts the same explicit versioning discipline.

### dev-experience

| Feature | Maturity | Future-proofing | Omni relevance | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Audit trail SPI | stable | 4/5 | adopt | `service-spi` |

**Audit trail SPI** — Hosts can receive a structured record of every mixin application decision (IMixinAuditTrail).

*Omni notes*: Wire it into the same audit store as FML-style class-transform logs: one queryable 'who changed this class' story (SOUL §16).

### extension

| Feature | Maturity | Future-proofing | Omni relevance | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Config plugins (runtime mod hooks) | core | 3/5 | adopt | `extensibility` |

**Config plugins (runtime mod hooks)** — Mods programmatically filter/augment their mixins at application time via IMixinConfigPlugin.

*Omni notes*: Must-support for compat; note it executes mod code inside the transformer — sandbox/observability accordingly.

## File Formats

### mixins.json (mixin config) (json)

- **Path pattern**: `<mod jar>/<name>.mixins.json (declared in the mod's manifest)`
- **Sources**: `transformer`, `mixin-wiki`

Per-mod config: 'package' root, mixin class lists split by side (mixins/client/server),
'required', 'priority' and 'mixinPriority', 'plugin' (IMixinConfigPlugin class), 'refmap',
'minVersion', 'compatibilityLevel', injector defaults (maxShiftBy etc.), and 'overwrites'
policy. Both loader families reference these from their own manifests (fabric.mod.json
'mixins' / FML advice provider) — Omni's canonical mod model needs a shared mixin-config slot.

### Reference map (refmap JSON) (json)

- **Path pattern**: `<mod jar>/<config>-refmap.json (generated at build time)`
- **Sources**: `refmap`, `mixin-wiki`

Generated mapping: per-mixin-class dictionaries from source-form target strings to
runtime-namespace descriptors, with per-environment sections ('mappings' plus named 'data'
variants). The binding between a compiled mod and its ecosystem's name universe — the object
of translation in any cross-ecosystem host.

## Analysis Notes

### Mixin is infrastructure, not a dependency

Every corpus loader ships and integrates Mixin rather than treating it as an ordinary library:
Fabric pins a fork (0.8.7 line — matching this repo's buildVersion), Quilt inherits that
integration, FML wires it through advice providers into the ClassProcessor pipeline. OmniLoader
therefore treats Mixin as core infrastructure: one bundled, pinned runtime + MixinServiceOmni +
audit integration, serving native mods and all hosted ecosystems uniformly. The fork/pin
decision flagged in the fabric-loader dossier is confirmed as a Phase 3 ADR item.

*Sources*: `service-spi`, `gradle-props`

### Version note at pin

buildVersion=0.8.7 (gradle.properties) — the same 0.8.7 line the ecosystem ships. Upstream
SpongePowered releases move slowly; the ecosystem's practical HEAD lives in loader forks
(Fabric's 0.17.3+mixin.0.8.7). MIT-licensed, in-repo docs/ and wiki are comprehensive.

*Sources*: `gradle-props`, `mixin-wiki`
